claim: Across syllables, non-identical homorganic labial-labial and coronal-coronal consonant pairs are generally underrepresented relative to expectation.

source_forms.pattern: low O/E in homorganic labial and coronal cells

normalized_environment: C1,C2 same major place -> underrepresentation tendency
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The restriction is not categorical and differs strongly by consonant identity, manner, and order.

claim: Segment order strongly conditions labial co-occurrence: in all roots /m-p/ and /m-f/ have O/E .52 and .77, but the reversed /p-m/ and /f-m/ have O/E 0.00.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The asymmetry partly tracks independent positional preferences rather than a pure pairwise order constraint.

claim: Much of the apparent order effect in homorganic sequences is attributed to independent positional biases: bilabials prefer initial syllables and coronal sonorants prefer non-initial syllables.
normalized_environment: pair order effect partly mediated by segment-position preferences
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors do not reduce all order effects to position; unexplained cells remain.

claim: The /m-v/ zero in the disyllabic sample is explicitly treated as potentially accidental because /v/ is the least frequent consonant; in the larger all-root sample /m-v/ is attested but still underrepresented (O/E .27).

source_forms.qualification: disyllabic zero may just be a random gap

normalized_environment: m...v absent in disyllabic sample but attested in all roots; accidental-gap candidate for zero cell
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The larger sample directly shows that the disyllabic zero is not an exceptionless lexical ban.

claim: Coronal co-occurrence is manner-sensitive: pairs of two coronal obstruents or two coronal sonorants are substantially more restricted than mixed-sonorancy coronal pairs.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The effect is gradient and individual pairs differ; /s-n/ is noted as a middle-ground case.

claim: For mixed-sonorancy coronal pairs, order follows the non-initial preference of coronal sonorants: /n-t n-s l-t l-s/ have lower O/E than the reverse orders /t-n s-n t-l s-l/.
normalized_environment: coronal sonorant favored as C2 rather than C1 in mixed-sonorancy pairs
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This is probabilistic; all listed nonzero combinations occur.

claim: The /n-v/ pair is an explicit unexplained sample-sensitive anomaly: O/E is 0.0 in disyllabic roots but 1.73 in the larger all-root dataset.
normalized_environment: n...v distribution unstable across root-length samples
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors state that they have no explanation for the contrast and do not generalize it.

claim: Nasal sequences beginning with /ŋ/ are restricted asymmetrically: /ŋ...m/ has all-root O/E 0, while /ŋ...n/ is low in disyllables (.33) but approximately expected in all roots (1.02).
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The higher all-root /ŋ...n/ value is explicitly treated as possibly anomalous.

claim: The velar/glottal pair /ŋ...ʔ/ and its reverse are unusually underrepresented (all-root O/E .51 and .25), which the authors connect to their historical homorganicity in Proto-Polynesian.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The restriction is stronger in disyllabic roots but still gradient; the explanation depends on historical place relations, not just synchronic segment labels.

claim: Summed homorganic counts show a strong manner effect: among labial homorganic pairs there are 27 total non-identical tokens but only 6 same-sonorancy tokens; among coronals there are 159 total but only 10 same-sonorancy tokens.
normalized_environment: same-sonorancy subset sharply depleted within homorganic pairs
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Labials show an order asymmetry: all six same-sonorancy labial occurrences fall in one order category because they all involve initial /m/.

claim: Homorganic avoidance is stronger for labials than coronals: six of twelve possible non-identical labial combinations have O/E 0, whereas only two coronal combinations approach zero; mixed-manner coronals often approach O/E 1.

source_forms.summary: labials: 6/12 nonidentical ordered pairs O/E=0; coronals: only 2 near 0

normalized_environment: OCP strength: labial > coronal, with coronal manner conditioning
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Different-manner labials range 0-.77 rather than approaching 1, while different-manner coronals are often much less restricted.
